CANARA HSBC LIFE INSURANCE | H1 FY27 INVESTOR UPDATE

Financial Performance
- Individual WPI ₹11,167 Mn, up 15% YoY.
- Total APE ₹12,497 Mn, up 14% YoY.
- Renewal premium ₹27,583 Mn, up 18% YoY.

Business & Distribution
- Gross premium ₹80,275 Mn in FY26.
- Five-year gross premium CAGR stood at 19%.
- Branch footprint expanded to 34 locations.
- Agency sales force crossed 1,900 people.
- Agency channel contributed ₹407 Mn APE in H1.
- Targeting rural and semi-urban markets with low penetration.

Operating Metrics
- 13th-month persistency improved to 85.6%.
- Solvency ratio stood at 180.4%.
- Claim settlement ratio stood at 96%.
- Reported expense ratio at 19.2% versus 18.5% YoY.

Strategic Priorities
- Focus on profitable growth and balanced product mix.
- Protection products support a higher traditional product mix.
- Expand distribution through Canara Bank and agency networks.
- Deploy AI and analytics to improve customer experience.
- GenAI tools target faster issuance and automated quality checks.
- AI-powered underwriting aims to improve speed and accuracy.
- Digital initiatives target better engagement and persistency.

Growth Opportunities
- Low insurance penetration offers long-term growth potential.
- Rising working-age population supports insurance demand.
- Retirement products offer an underpenetrated opportunity.
- Retail lending growth supports credit-life insurance demand.
- Rural expansion could unlock a large customer base.

KEY TAKEAWAY
- VNB grew 24%, with margins improving to 21.3%.
- Renewal premium and AUM showed healthy growth.
- Persistency and solvency remain important operating indicators.
- Distribution expansion and AI adoption support future growth.
- Monitor profitability, expense ratio and new-business momentum.

**TCS | Q2 FY27 BROKER REPORT | BUY | TP ₹2,390**

**Revenue + Growth**
- PL maintains BUY with revised target of ₹2,390.
- Earlier target price stood at ₹2,580.
- Q2 revenue grew 0.5% QoQ in CC.
- Growth was broadly in line with estimates.
- International revenue increased 1.2% QoQ in CC.
- BFSI grew 2.5% QoQ in CC.
- Manufacturing grew 3.1% QoQ in CC.
- Technology & Services grew 3.1% QoQ in CC.
- Consumer and ERU segments continued declining.

**AI + Deal Wins**
- Annualized AI revenue reached US$3.1 Bn.
- AI revenue accounts for around 10% of revenue.
- AI revenue increased 19.2% QoQ.
- TCV reached US$9.6 Bn.
- TCV excludes major Porsche and Best Buy deals.
- AI traction supports long-term growth opportunities.
- Healthy deal pipeline supports revenue visibility.

**Margins + Cost Pressures**
- EBIT margin stood at 24.0%.
- Margin missed PL estimates by 40 bps.
- AI investments increased operating expenses.
- Strategic partnerships and M&A added costs.
- Higher bench and subcontracting costs pressured margins.
- MHP integration may dilute margins by 50 bps.
- Long-term margin aspiration remains unchanged at 26%.

**Revenue Estimates**
- FY27E revenue growth revised to 3.4%.
- Earlier FY27E growth estimate was 2.9%.
- FY28E revenue growth revised to 5.0%.
- Earlier FY28E growth estimate was 3.6%.
- MHP contribution expected from Q4FY27E.
- Organic growth expected to improve modestly in H2.

**Margin Estimates**
- FY27E EBIT margin revised to 24.0%.
- Earlier FY27E margin estimate was 24.6%.
- FY28E EBIT margin revised to 24.2%.
- Earlier FY28E margin estimate was 24.8%.
- Q2 margin miss impacted revised estimates.
- MHP integration adds near-term margin pressure.

**Long-Term Outlook**
- Organic USD revenue CAGR projected at 3.0%.
- INR PAT CAGR projected at 6.6%.
- Forecast period covers FY27-FY29E.
- AI transformation offers potential growth opportunities.
- Continued investment supports long-term competitiveness.

**Valuation + Key Metrics**
- Target values TCS at 14x Sept. 2028E EPS.
- Earlier valuation multiple stood at 15x.
- FY28E EPS estimated at ₹165.6.
- FY28E EV/Sales estimated at 2.2x.
- FY28E EV/EBITDA estimated at 8.5x.
- FY28E P/E estimated at 12.5x.
- FY28E dividend yield estimated at 7.2%.

**Workforce + Attrition**
- Headcount increased by 4,300 employees.
- Total workforce reached approximately 5.98 lakh.
- Attrition declined 30 bps QoQ to 13.3%.
- Stable attrition supports workforce continuity.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
PL retains BUY on TCS with a reduced ₹2,390 target. Strong AI revenue, broad-based growth in key verticals and healthy deal wins support the outlook. However, margin pressure from investments and MHP integration has reduced earnings estimates and valuation multiples. The 26% long-term margin aspiration remains intact.

reports.text:
HOSPITAL STOCKS ; 30% MARGIN CAP ON CANCER DRUGS 

• Trade margin rationalisation proposed for non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs.

• Trade margins to be capped at 30% of Maximum Retail Price (MRP).

• Average trade mark-up on non-scheduled cancer drugs is nearly 170%, with some reaching up to 700%.

• Proposed cap could lead to significant price reductions, potentially up to 70% of MRP for certain drugs.

• Estimated annual savings from the 30% margin cap could reach ₹2,500 crore.

• Analysts believe the 30% cap is more favourable for the industry than the previously debated 16% margin cap.

• Hospital companies could face an estimated 1–4% EBITDA impact.

• Pharma companies may continue selling drugs at existing prices, limiting the direct impact on manufacturers.

• Matter remains sub judice, with the next court update expected on October 12.

Impact:

🔴 Hospitals — Negative: Potential pressure on pharmacy margins and EBITDA.

🟡 Pharma — Neutral to Mildly Negative: Impact depends on existing distribution margins and pricing arrangements.

INDIAN MARKET – THIS IS NOT A BEAR MARKET

Key Points
- Sensex hit its latest peak on 26 Sep 2024
- By 1 Oct 2026, Sensex had fallen over 16%
- Current decline ranks 17th among top 20 Sensex falls
- Decline has lasted over 740 days
- It is the second-longest decline in the top 20
- Longest decline lasted 814 days from 1994–1996
- That 1994–96 fall was nearly 41%
- Current decline is therefore long but relatively shallow
- Market can be described as sideways or stagnant
- Author argues this is not a bear market

NIFTY 500 TRI
- Last all-time closing high: 24 Sep 2024
- Trough reached on 28 Feb 2025
- Peak-to-trough fall was nearly 19%
- As of 6 Oct 2026, index was ~7.6% below peak

Key Takeaway
- Current market weakness has been unusually prolonged
- However, the decline remains relatively shallow
- The author characterises it as a sideways market
- Conclusion: This is not a bear market

This strategic collaboration integrates Claude into Hexaware's AI-native platforms, Zerovity™ and Agentverse™, enhancing their ability to deliver outcome-based AI services for enterprises. 

This partnership is significant as it allows clients to leverage Claude's capabilities to address technical challenges and optimize business processes effectively.

- Claude will also enhance Agentverse™, which features over 600 pre-built agents. 
- Clients can utilize Hexaware’s zero friction enterprise™ offerings to tackle technical debt, security vulnerabilities, and process bottlenecks.

reports.text:
India produces more milk than any country in world but still buys 85% of its whey protein powder from other countries 

This happens because whey comes from cheese making and India never built big cheese factories. Price of imported whey powder went from ₹700 per kg in 2024 to ₹3,000 per kg in 2026 t hat means companies making protein shakes in India now pay 3 to 4 times more for their main ingredient. 

Some Indian dairy companies like Parag Milk Foods are now trying to make whey inside India

Hindustan Unilever just launched Horlicks Protein Powder but instead of using whey, it uses protein made from yeast through fermentation. Yeast protein does not need imports and can be produced inside India 

Marico paid ₹225 crore to buy 60% of Cosmix, which also sells yeast based protein products. Both companies are not just selling protein to more people. They are changing what protein powder is made from. 

By moving away from expensive imported whey, they control costs and do not depend on foreign suppliers

India protein product market is worth ₹7,000 crore but only 3% of households buy protein products. About 73% of city living Indians do not get enough protein and 93% do not even know how much protein their body needs daily. 

Cosmix, which Marico just bought, grew from ₹24 crore revenue in FY24 to ₹50 crore in FY25 and now runs at ₹100 crore yearly pace. When big companies like HUL and Marico enter with their distribution reach, more households start buying

Indian Equity Valuations Cool Off From 2024 Highs

Indian market valuations have reset meaningfully from their 2024 peak, according to Motilal Oswal.

Large-cap and mid-cap valuations have corrected 31% and 36%, respectively, while small-caps have seen a relatively modest 7% correction on 12-month forward P/E.

The Nifty now trades at an 18% discount to its long-period average (LPA), a sharp reversal from the 20% premium in September 2024.

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.

Is India investing enough for future capacity

India is usually described as a consumption economy. Consumption contributes >60% of GDP. But the story becomes incomplete when we ignore what's happening on the investment side and other aspects of our economy

India's Gross Capital Formation is ~32.6% of GDP. Lower than China's ~40%, but China's per capita GDP is several times of India's. Comparing ratios without considering income levels misses the context.

A developing country cannot allocate every ₹ toward factories & infra. A large share of resources must also support the bottom of the pyramid through housing, healthcare, education & welfare.

A harmonious society requires a minimum standard of living for those at the bottom. India is building capacity while simultaneously funding social stability. That's a tougher balancing act than many realize.

So let's move beyond GDP narratives & look at hard physical data. India's share of global GDP is only ~3.5% yet produces roughly 10% of the world's steel. Steel almost 3x our weight in global GDP. Steel isn't consumed for consumption's sake, but goes into factories, rail tracks, power plants, ports, airports, infrastructure etc

Cement tells the same story. India produces ~400 MT annually out of ~4,000 MT globally. Again, roughly 10% global share despite only ~3.5% share of world GDP. Countries don't consume steel & cement at this scale unless they are building physical assets. These are the raw materials of future GDP.

Power generation presents a slightly different picture. India's share of global electricity output is lower than steel & cement, but still materially ahead of its global GDP share. India with 1800bn units vs 32,000bn units, 6% global share

The evidence suggests India is investing for future capability. One may argue the investment cycle started later than it should have, but the direction is unmistakable. Steel, Cement & Power share point toward economy preparing for a much larger future.

The scale of projects are also changing. DFCs, industrial corridors, semiconductor fabs, renewable energy parks, metros, airports, transmission corridors & logistics networks are larger than anything India attempted before.

If this trend continues, India's share of global steel, cement & power usage is likely to keep rising. Higher material intensity today is often a precursor to higher economic output tomorrow.

Maybe the better way to describe India isn't "consumption economy." It's a country simultaneously consuming, uplifting millions & building future productive capacity. 
India need a balancing act of Building future and taking care of the needy, which it is working towards

De-Dollarization lets peek into central bank reserves

Central banks are diversifying but US$ isn't giving up the throne anytime soon. Headlines scream de-dollarization bt US$ still makes up ~57% of global FX reserves. That's down from decades ago, but still miles ahead of everyone else.

Euro is the 2nd largest reserve currency at ~20%. But Europe faces weak growth, aging demographics, fiscal stress & fragmented politics. Hence no comfort for people looking to diversify away from US$

Then its China. Despite its economic size, RMB is only ~2% of global reserves & ~2% of global payments. Clear reflection of trust issues with the dragon. deep capital markets, convertibility & rule of law issues also there

They're moving into something with no issuer at all: Gold. Central banks themselves are now one of the biggest sources of gold demand globally, roughly buy ~30% of annual global mine production

Gold isn't rising only because investors are bullish. Significant chunk of global prodn is locked away by sovereign balance sheets. In 2026, central banks gold buying at slower pace vs 2025 due to 60% price rise.

Among the Major buyers were Poland, China, Brazil, India etc. 
Then there are few sellers too. Turkey has been among the largest sellers this year, reportedly selling ~83t YTD to support liquidity & FX/US$ needs.

That’s the problem. Though world want to move away from US$ in the long term but  issue in the medium term created due to lack of US$ in the country. 
Case in point Turkiye

Russia has also been a notable seller, reducing reserves by ~44t YTD as it seeks hard-currency liquidity. But Russia is also large producer of Gold

Gold is becoming a reserve diversification asset in a world where trust in fiat issuers is fragmenting.
BUT de-dollarization in reserves doesn't mean de-dollarization in trade.
That’s two very different thing

Global trade still run on the USD infrastructure. That network effect is incredibly hard to replace.
So its two-step process. Trade continues in USD.
But exporting nations convert a portion of their accumulated surplus reserves into gold, commodities, sovereign funds or other reserve assets.

The world may keep transacting in dollars while increasingly choosing not to store all its savings in dollars.

Conclusion:
Real story is different from "the end of the USD."
Reserve diversification is real.
Dollar replacement is not. Not in near future

Birla trying to replicate Paint like disruption in Wire & Cables
India's W&C industry is a INR 1.1trn & growing at ~13% CAGR. Despite its size (0.3% of India GDP), industry remains fragmented with top 6 players control ~50% share

Market is roughly split into 3 equal buckets: Wires, LT Cables & MV/HT/EHV/Specialized Cables. Cables compared to wire is more organized, house wires have larger unorganized participation. Overall unorganized is > 30%

what attracted Birla. W&C sits at the intersection of electrification, urbanization & digitization. Housing, infra, renewables, data centres & manufacturing all need more wires.

Ultratech has launched Ultravolt with planned capex of ₹18 bn. Initial plant capacity has already started production ahead of schedule at Bharuch. The market compares this with the paint disruption. Lets look at numbers

Grasim's paint capex was ~65-70% of Asian Paint. Ultravolt's ₹18 bn capex is 30% of Polycab gross block. Plus, Polycab's gross block is expected to reach ~₹94 bn in FY28 while KEI could reach ~₹43 bn. Ultravolt's announced gross block is only ₹18 bn

The biggest advantage for Ultratech is raw material availability. Copper & Aluminium dominate industry economics and the Birla ecosystem already has deep expertise & inhouse production

Demand-intelligence advantage. Cement is purchased 6 months before wires in building construction. Ultratech can potentially spot demand trends 4-6 months ahead of competitors

Builder relationships, contractor network & Ultratech Building Solutions outlets create a ready-made ecosystem for cross-selling wires. That's a powerful advantage most new entrant

Ultravolt has prepared well. Better channel incentives, faster delivery commitments, aggressive marketing & strong retailer engagement are already creating buzz. But replicating the paint playbook won't be straightforward. 

Paints & cement share significant overlap in distribution. Wires are largely sold through electrical dealers, distributors, retailers & electrician networks. Building an electrical distribution franchise takes years

Another key difference is profitability. Leading W&C players operate at ~12-14% EBITDA margins, far lower than the 18-20%+ margins paint Co. enjoyed before disruption. With lower margins, room for aggressive pricing is limited

Further: Utility, industrial, railway, transmission & infra projects require extensive testing, approvals, certifications & execution history before meaningful scale can be achieved.
Conclusion: Birla has genuine advantage in raw material sourcing, builder relationships & demand visibility. But unlike paints, incumbents start with lower margins, stronger technical moats & entrenched distribution

Jury is still out. Ultravolt looks prepared. Space will remain interesting

Coforge Chairman resignation : Lets dig deeper

OP Bhatt's resignation came after disagreements around the Board evaluation process. In his resignation note, he says continuing on Board amid differences regarding his "good faith actions" would not be conducive to Board effective functioning 

OP Bhatt is not a conventional IT industry chairman. He is among India's most respected bankers, having led SBI between 2006-11 & later served on boards across large corporates including Tata Group companies

The market doesn’t take such update kindly, but Bhatt's continuation was already under question even before the resignation. Shareholders (inc largest shareholder Advent) voted against his reappointment as Independent Director from May'27
 
Let’s go a bit in history: The company was earlier known as NIIT Tech before its ownership transition & eventual rebranding to Coforge. Barings acquired control of NIIT in 2020, leading to ownership change then.

Later, Barings steadily monetised its stake through multiple block deals as the company scaled in size, profitability & market value. After Barings' complete exit by FY24, Co. become fully public market institutional owned.

OP Bhatt joined the board in 2024 & became Chairman during a phase when Coforge was pursuing aggressive scale-up ambitions. Coforge accelerated inorganic growth. The acquisition of Cigniti significantly expanded its engineering & digital capabilities under him.

The much bigger acquisition Encora was also under OP Bhatt. The acquisition materially increased Coforge's scale, global delivery footprint & exposure to high-growth digital engineering segments.

Encora also changed the shareholding landscape. Through the transaction, Advent became the largest shareholder in Coforge, making its views impossible for the board to ignore. That's why the key takeaway may not be the resignation itself. The bigger story could be that the largest shareholder & the Chairman were not aligned on important matters. 

The bullish view is that management execution remains intact. The cautious view is that whenever Chairman, Board & largest shareholder are not on the same page, governance questions emerge and mgmt. energy is focussed away from growth.
